text:
sam: noticed staging heap on gpu0 creeping up during long perf runs after the kv-cache change. not steady OOM but resident increases over hours.

 taylor: hmm fragmentation vs true leak? did you compare allocator free lists/heap histos between start/end?

 sam: i pulled nsys snapshots and a few allocator dumps. attaching quick logs: 
```
nvprof: device approx used 38.7GB -> 42.1GB over 6h, no single allocation spikes.
/var/log/runtime/alloc-stats-1823.txt: slab_total=41943040 slabs_in_use=324 free_chunks=12345 kvcache_resident=243MB
```

 maria: can you paste the runtime /metrics output (allocator counters)? also what model/config were you running (seq len, batch distribution)?

 sam: model=redwood/v1-small quant=fp16 seq=2048 typical batch sizes burst to 8 then settle at 2, sustained throughput ~120 tok/s. metrics snapshot: 
```
allocator.alloc_calls: 125432
allocator.free_calls: 125400
allocator.peak_resident: 42949672960
allocator.current_resident: 43876219392
kvcache.entries: 1240
kvcache.evictions: 312
```

 akash: free_calls nearly matches allocs but resident rising — classic fragmentation. but nvprof shows many small persistent buffers ~64-512KB that never get coalesced. did we change slab bucket sizes in last allocator tuning patch? @taylor

 taylor: yes, last week's patch added an extra 256KB slab class to reduce splintering for model weights. maybe some code path allocated from new slab and never returned properly when kvcache evicted entries. could be an unref in kv-evict path.

 sam: i wrote a small repro that mimics kvcache churn + inference worker pooling. script runs 2k evictions/hour and tracks cudaMemory usage: 
```
# repro_kv_eviction.py (excerpt)
for i in range(10000):
    key = f"k{i%2000}"
    kv.set(key, gen_random_kv_blob())
    if random.random() < 0.15:
        kv.evict_lru()
    if i % 500 == 0:
        runtime.flush_workspaces()
    time.sleep(0.01)
```

 maria: ran repro on my laptop instance, reproduced steady growth after ~40m. took nsys timeline and ran our allocator debug: 
```
ALLOC_DEBUG=1 RUNTIME_SLAB_LOG=1 python repro_kv_eviction.py --workers=4
```

 buildbot: nightly job 2026-03-16/03:00 produced similar graph and attached heap snapshot: s3://redwood-internal/profiler/heap-182345-snapshot.nsp. job note: "resident grew 3.8GB in 3h"

 akash: can someone grep for missing decref in kv eviction code? suspect path: storage/kv_cache.cc: evict_ent -> remove_kv_buffers -> schedule_free but missing release of workspace ref when eviction races with worker reuse. racey but reproducible with bursting batches.

 taylor: added an assert/trace in local branch to log workspace refcounts on evict. output shows refcount stuck at 1 after remove_kv_buffers sometimes. push patch to add explicit workspace->release() on evict fallback. will run CI with repro harness.

 sam: after applying explicit release i re-ran repro for 2h, resident stable (delta < 20MB). nvprof now shows fewer orphaned 256KB buffers.

 maria: good candidate for postmortem and writeup. also opened perf ticket with kernel selection note: the extra 256KB slab helped batch perf but amplified leak when it existed. we should add allocator health check in console and an eviction-time sanity check metric (orphaned_buffers).

 akash: filing follow-up: - revert to safe slab sizing on canary if orphan metric > 0.05% - add RT test that churns kv entries under bursty batches - add telemetry for slab occupancy by bucket.

 sam: thanks. saved a lot of time with repro script. attaching link to branch with repro and fix: gitlab.com/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/4823 (please review). :thumbsup:

 taylor: will merge after CI. great sleuthing team. :party_parrot:
